latest.title: Qué es Knowledge Driven Development y por qué la IA lo necesita
latest.description:
Knowledge Driven Development es una práctica de desarrollo de software donde el conocimiento del proyecto se estructura, versiona y utiliza como contexto activo para humanos, equipos y agentes de IA.
Su objetivo no es crear documentación pesada, sino mantener la mínima información suficiente para tomar mejores decisiones, reducir ambigüedad y mejorar la colaboración entre negocio, tecnología e inteligencia artificial.

latest.title: Cross-Region Inference and Canadian Data Residency: What You Actually Need to Know
latest.description: No Canadian law — federal or provincial — explicitly prohibits transient cross-border AI inference. The widespread belief that "Canadian data must stay in Canada" is a misinterpretation of accountability-based frameworks that regulate *how* you protect data, not *where* computation physically occurs. With Amazon Bedrock Guardrails stripping PII before inference and CRIS creating zero persistent data in destination regions, the compliance question shifts from geography to architecture.

trending.title: AIdeas Finalist: ASET – Academic Safety and Evidencing Truth
trending.description:
ASET (Academic Safety and Evidencing Truth) is a scientific claim verification engine built  for the AI era — where information can be generated instantly, but trust cannot, to address the growing problem of hallucinated citations and  AI-generated information.

Instead of probabilistic prediction, ASET retrieves, analyzes, and synthesizes evidence from 1.2M+ indexed research papers to produce literature-backed verification reports for claims extracted from text, documents, webpages, images, and videos.

trending.title: Is Node.js Still Enough? When to Move Your Backend to Rust
trending.description: Node.js remains the king of rapid development and I/O-bound tasks, but its single-threaded event loop chokes on heavy computation, while V8 garbage collection can introduce unpredictable latency spikes at scale. The answer isn't a total rewrite—it’s a hybrid architecture. Keep Node.js for your API gateway and CRUD operations, and offload CPU-heavy bottlenecks to specialized Rust microservices.
